title: Particles, Localization and "Collapse"
abstract: Hegerfeldt's theorem shows that the localization of a particle (or field) is not possible under very general assumptions of quantum mechanics and special relativity. This theorem, and further developments and associated theorems force penetrating questions on the proper understanding of the theory and its use. In particular, the use of the collapse postulate is called into question. The existence of particles and even localized fields are called into question. And, this in turn challenges local measurements. It generally forces one to consider the profound problems and even wrong results that arise from the collapse postulate. We give a qualitatively new example of such a wrong result. Researchers and students alike are bothered by these fundamental issues. Students' ability to learn the material, and even their interest in physics, can be compromised by such disturbing conundra that seem to make physics, or at least QFT and its QM limit, seem incomprehensible and even inconsistent. This article resolves these issues in a way accessible to undergraduates, by applying the natural (minimal) interpretation of quantum mechanics (QM) (the ensemble interpretation) and explicating and clarifying the basic principles and premises used in QM and the Hegerfeldt theorem and its application to measurements.
summary: This paper critically examines the 'collapse postulate' of quantum mechanics, arguing it is inconsistent with relativistic principles like causality and localization. It proposes an 'ensemble interpretation' as a more natural framework that explains quantum phenomena, such as interference, without invoking instantaneous wave function collapses.
main_problem: The paper questions the fundamental validity of the quantum mechanical 'collapse postulate' when reconciling quantum mechanics with special relativity and localization principles.
main_result: The collapse postulate is shown to be inconsistent with fundamental principles like causality and localization limits derived from special relativity, suggesting an alternative ensemble interpretation is necessary.
method: The analysis compares the predictions of the standard collapse interpretation against those derived from the unitary Schrödinger Equation evolution, using the two-slit experiment as a primary test case.
model_or_system: The discussion centers on quantum particles and fields, using the two-slit experiment and the mathematical framework of wave function evolution (Schrödinger Equation) versus instantaneous state jumps (collapse postulate).
key_observables: Interference patterns, wavefunction localization, and the probability of measurement outcomes.
important_parameters: The assumptions of special relativity and the requirement for causality are central constraints.
main_assumptions: The paper critiques the assumption that the collapse postulate is a fundamental, necessary component of quantum mechanics.
figures_summary: The notes reference a schematic of the two-slit experiment, illustrating the contrast between the standard collapse model and the implications of wave function behavior.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the conflict between localization and relativity (Hegerfeldt's theorem), then contrasting the standard collapse view with the ensemble interpretation, and finally demonstrating inconsistencies in the collapse model using experimental analogies.
why_interesting: This is highly relevant as it tackles the foundational interpretation of quantum mechanics, which underpins all advanced topics in quantum physics, including open quantum systems and measurement theory.
